content.value_statement: Rust projects can become difficult to test and maintain as crates and dependencies grow. This skill provides practical patterns for workspace structure, boundaries, testing, tracing, and quality gates.
actual_capabilities: Proposes workspace layouts with clear core, adapter, application, and binary boundaries.
Explains shared Cargo dependency management and feature design.
Recommends Rust visibility and error-handling patterns for library and binary crates.
Designs layered unit, integration, end-to-end, property, and fuzz testing strategies.
Recommends tracing, Clippy, formatting, and dependency-audit quality gates.
limitations: Does not inspect or modify a repository unless the host agent provides those capabilities.
Does not replace project-specific performance profiling or security review.
Dependency versions and tool compatibility require verification against the current Rust ecosystem.
Guidance is general and may need adjustment for embedded, WebAssembly, or regulated systems.

use_cases.title: Design a new workspace
use_cases.description: Create a small Cargo workspace with deliberate crate boundaries and shared dependencies.

use_cases.title: Refactor a growing service
use_cases.description: Separate domain logic from adapters and reduce dependency coupling in an existing Rust service.

use_cases.title: Strengthen delivery checks
use_cases.description: Define repeatable tests, linting, formatting, and dependency checks for a Rust CI pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a starter workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Cargo workspace for a Rust CLI and library. Explain each crate and its dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Improve crate boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust workspace layout and recommend boundaries between core logic, adapters, and application code: [layout].

prompt_templates.title: Create a test strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a layered Rust testing strategy for this service. Include unit, integration, end-to-end, and property tests: [service description].

prompt_templates.title: Audit engineering practices
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Rust project against senior practices for dependencies, features, errors, tracing, and CI. Prioritize changes with reasons: [project details].

output_examples.input: Design a workspace for an API service with PostgreSQL storage.
output: Recommended crates: core, adapters, app, and api binary.
Keep database code in adapters behind a trait boundary.
Run formatting, Clippy, tests, and dependency checks in CI.

output_examples.input: Improve test coverage for a parsing library.
output: Keep deterministic parser tests near the implementation.
Add public API integration tests under the crate tests directory.
Use property tests and fuzzing for untrusted input formats.

best_practices: Keep domain logic independent from network, database, and filesystem adapters.
Pin the Rust toolchain and verify the minimum supported Rust version in CI.
Use small public APIs and test behavior at each system boundary.
anti_patterns: Do not split a project into many crates before clear boundaries exist.
Do not expose all modules publicly for convenience.
Do not rely only on end-to-end tests for core business logic.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Rust developers who need maintainable workspace and production engineering guidance.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides recommendations and examples for an agent or developer to apply.

faq.question: Does it support single-crate projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The principles also help organize a single Rust crate before it needs a workspace.

faq.question: Does it recommend specific dependencies?
faq.answer: It discusses common tools, but you should verify current versions and suitability.

faq.question: Can it help with CI?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends formatting, linting, testing, and dependency audit quality gates.

faq.question: Does it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. Dependency tools and engineering practices complement a dedicated security review.
